newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Saudi could take 35 pct of Petrogal - Portugal.
newsitem.headline: Saudi could take 35 pct of Petrogal - Portugal.

text.p: Saudi Aramco could take a stake of up to 35 percent in Portuguese state oil company Petrogal-Petroleos de Portugal, Portugal's Secretary of State for Industry and Energy Jose Penedos said.
Penedos told Reuters that negotiations could be concluded by the end of the year.

"It could be slightly more (than 30 percent) but with an upper limit of 35 percent," he said. "The conditions are right for reaching an agreement but we're not talking about everything being finalised yet," he said.
In July Aramco and Petrogal signed a non-binding memorandum of understanding to assess the possibility of setting up a partnership.
An analysis conducted by Merrill Lynch valued Petrogal at between 230 and 280 billion escudos.
Penedos said he was less confident that Angolan oil company Sonangol would take a direct stake.
"If it were too early for Sonangol to make a decision like this we could find another solution. It could perhaps take a stake in a Petrogal subsidiary," said Penedos.
But he said negotiations were still concentrated on the possibility of Sonangol taking a direct stake of between five and 10 percent.

Angolan Petroleum Minister Albina Assis Africano, who was on a visit to Oporto for the inauguration of a specialist training course for engineers, said such a decision would depend on the results of a financial analysis of both companies.
The Portuguese state currently holds 55 percent of Petrogal while private shareholders of the Petrocontrol group hold the remaining 45 percent.
